title: Rising above every other master
source_text: Πολλῶν τοίνυν λεγομένων ἢ ὄντων θεῶν ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ κυρίων, ἡμεῖς πάντα πράττομεν, ἵν᾿ οὐ μόνα τὰ προσκυνούμενα ὡς θεοὺς παρὰ τοῖς ἐπὶ γῆς ἔθνεσιν ὑπεραναβῶμεν ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ οὕς φασιν αἱ γραφαὶ θεοὺς, περὶ ὧν οὐδὲν ἴσασιν οἱ „ξένοι τῶν“ διὰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ ἡμῶν „διαθηκῶν“ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀλλότριοι τῶν διὰ τούτων δηλουμένων ἐπαγγελιῶν αὐτοῦ. ὑπεραναβαίνει δὲ τὴν παρὰ πᾶσι δαιμονίοις δουλείαν ὁ μηδὲν ἔργον δαιμονίοις φίλον ποιῶν, καὶ ὑπεραναβαίνει τὴν μερίδα τῶν παρὰ Παύλῳ λεγομένων εἶναι θεῶν ὁ σκοπῶν, εἴτε ὡς ἐκεῖνοι εἴθ᾿ ὅπως ποτὲ ἔχει τὰ πράγματα, οὐ „τὰ βλεπόμενα ἀλλὰ τὰ μὴ βλεπόμενα“· καὶ ὁρῶν τις, τίνα τρόπον καὶ „ἡ τῆς κτίσεως ἀποκαραδοκία τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται,“ „οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα ἐπ᾿ ἐλπίδι,“ εὐφημῶν τὴν κτίσιν καὶ βλέπων, τίνα τρόπον „ἐλευθερωθήσεται“ πᾶσα „ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς“ καὶ καταντήσεται „εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ θεοῦ,“ οὐ περισπᾶται πρὸς (τὸ) τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἄλλῳ τινὶ δουλεύειν μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ πρὸς τὸ „δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν.“ οὐ στάσεως οὖν φωνὴ ἐπὶ τοῖς νοήσασι τὰ τοιαῦτα καὶ μὴ θέλουσι „δουλεύειν“ πλείοσι „κυρίοις,“ διὰ τοῦτο ἀρκουμένοις κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, παιδεύοντι ὑφ᾿ ἑαυτῷ τοὺς δουλεύοντας αὐτῷ, ἵν᾿ αὐτοὺς πεπαιδευμένους παραδῷ γενομένους „βασιλείαν“ ἀξίαν θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί. ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀποσχίζουσι καὶ ἀποῤῥηγνύουσιν ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων „τῆς πολιτείας“ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ξένων „τῶν διαθηκῶν“ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα „τὸ ἐν οὐρανοῖς πολίτευμα“ πολιτεύσωνται, προσερχόμενοι θεῷ ζῶντι „καὶ πόλει θεοῦ, Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων πανηγύρει καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων, ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανῷ.“
pass_a_gloss: Many gods then being called (λεγόμενοι) or being (ὄντες), and likewise lords, we do (πράττω) all things so that we may climb above (ὑπεραναβαίνω) not only the things worshipped (προσκυνέω) as gods among the nations on earth but also those whom the writings (γραφαί) call gods, about whom those know nothing who are 'strangers (ξένος) to the covenants (διαθήκη)' of God through Moses and our Saviour (σωτήρ) Jesus, and aliens (ἀλλότριος) to his promises (ἐπαγγελία) made clear (δηλόω) through these. He climbs above the servitude (δουλεία) to all demons (δαιμόνιον) who does no work dear to demons; and he climbs above the portion (μερίς) of those said by Paul to be gods who looks at (σκοπέω), whether as those or however things stand, not 'the things seen but the things not seen'; and one seeing in what way 'the eager expectation (ἀποκαραδοκία) of the creation (κτίσις) awaits (ἀπεκδέχομαι) the revelation (ἀποκάλυψις) of the sons of God', 'not willing (ἑκών) but because of the one who subjected (ὑποτάσσω) [it] in hope (ἐλπίς)', speaking well of (εὐφημέω) the creation and seeing in what way all 'will be freed (ἐλευθερόω) from the bondage of corruption (φθορά)' and will arrive (καταντάω) 'into the freedom (ἐλευθερία) of the glory (δόξα) of the children (τέκνον) of God', is not drawn aside (περισπάω) to serving God and some other with him, nor to 'serving two lords'. Not then a voice of sedition in those who have understood (νοέω) such things and not wishing to 'serve' more 'lords', for this reason being content (ἀρκέομαι) with the Lord Jesus Christ, who trains/educates (παιδεύω) under himself those serving him, so that he may hand over (παραδίδωμι) them, trained, having become a 'kingdom (βασιλεία)' worthy of God, to the God and Father. But they also split themselves off (ἀποσχίζω) and break away (ἀπορρήγνυμι) from those alien 'to the commonwealth (πολιτεία)' of God and strangers 'to his covenants', so that they may live as citizens (πολιτεύομαι) 'the commonwealth (πολίτευμα) in the heavens', approaching (προσέρχομαι) the living God 'and the city of God, heavenly (ἐπουράνιος) Jerusalem, and myriads of angels, a festal assembly (πανήγυρις), and assembly (ἐκκλησία) of firstborn (πρωτότοκος) enrolled (ἀπογράφω) in heaven'.
pass_b_english: Since, then, there are many gods, whether so called or real, and likewise many lords, we do all we can to rise above not only the things worshipped as gods among the nations on earth, but also those whom the Scriptures call gods. About these they know nothing who are “strangers to the covenants” (Ephesians 2:12) of God given through Moses and through our Saviour Jesus, and who are aliens to His promises made known through these.

The one who does no work that is dear to demons rises above servitude to all demons. And the one who looks “not to the things that are seen but to the things that are not seen” (2 Corinthians 4:18), whether in the way those beings do or however the matter may stand, rises above the portion of those whom Paul says are gods. And when a man sees how “the eager longing of the creation waits for the revealing of the sons of God” (Romans 8:19), “not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it, in hope” (Romans 8:20); when he speaks of the creation with reverence and sees how all of it “will be set free from its bondage to corruption” and will come “into the freedom of the glory of the children of God” (Romans 8:21), he is not drawn away into serving God and some other being along with Him, nor into “serving two masters” (Matthew 6:24).

So it is not the voice of sedition in those who have understood such things and do not wish to “serve” several “masters,” and who for this reason are content with the Lord Jesus Christ. He trains under Himself those who serve Him, so that, when they have been trained and have become a “kingdom” worthy of God, He may hand them over to God the Father (1 Corinthians 15:24). Yet they do cut themselves off and break away from those who are aliens to “the commonwealth” of God and strangers to His “covenants” (Ephesians 2:12), so that they may live as citizens of “the commonwealth in heaven” (Philippians 3:20), drawing near to the living God “and to the city of God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in festal gathering, and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven” (Hebrews 12:22–23).

choices.choice: Ephesians 2:12 is used twice: first ξένοι τῶν διαθηκῶν, then, adapted, ἀλλοτρίων τῆς πολιτείας (Paul has ‘the commonwealth of Israel’; Origen writes ‘of God’). Romans 8:21: Paul has αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις; Origen’s πᾶσα (‘all of it’) echoes Romans 8:22; kept as he frames it. 1 Corinthians 15:24: only ‘kingdom’ is marked as quoted; the handing over to ‘God the Father’ is Origen’s paraphrase of the verse. Hebrews 12:22-23: Origen adapts the wording (‘drawing near to the living God’; ἐν οὐρανῷ for ἐν οὐρανοῖς). The phrase ‘the voice of sedition’ answers Celsus’s charge reported in 8.2. εἴτε ὡς ἐκεῖνοι εἴθ᾿ ὅπως ποτὲ ἔχει τὰ πράγματα is obscure: ἐκεῖνοι most likely means the ‘gods’ Paul speaks of (who themselves look to unseen things), with Origen leaving open how things stand with them; rendered ‘whether in the way those beings do or however the matter may stand’. The two ὑπεραναβαίνει sentences are put subject-first in English. Romans 8:20 is joined as Origen joins it, with no bridging verb added. διὰ τούτων (‘through these’) may mean the covenants or Moses and Jesus; left open. πλείοσι rendered ‘several’, as in 8.2. 1 Corinthians 15:24 has τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί verbatim. εὐφημῶν τὴν κτίσιν: ‘speaking well of / with reverence about the creation’ (i.e., not blaspheming it, as some heretics did). (τὸ) before τῷ θεῷ is Koetschau’s supplement, accepted. ‘whether so called or real’ renders λεγομένων ἢ ὄντων, picking up 1 Corinthians 8:5 from 8.4.

removed added 'having been subjected' before the Romans 8:20 quotation
removed added 'truly' in 'however the matter may stand' (ὅπως ποτέ)
'made known through these covenants' changed to 'through these' (διὰ τούτων left open)
